title.narrative: AFSA, Transforming the African Food System to Sustainability (TAFS)
AFSA, Transforming the African Food System to Sustainability (TAFS)

description.narrative:
The Alliance for Food Sovereignty in Africa (AFSA) is a broad alliance of civil society actors that are part of the struggle for food sovereignty and agroecology in Africa. Its members represent smallholder farmers, pastoralists, hunter/gatherers, indigenous peoples, faith-based institutions, and environmentalists from across Africa. It is a network of networks and currently with 35 active members. AFSA has a secretariat office in Kampala, Uganda, and a West Africa liaison office in Thies, Senegal. AFSA is a growing voice on the continent for sensible, sustainable, just, regenerative, and healthy food systems.
AFSA`s intervention aims to influence food policy makers' narratives locally and regionally through advocacy, ensuring that food policies are geared towards the health and well-being of African citizens. The intervention leverages on previous activities bringing all AFSA's work together and shifts the conversation away from food production to the systemic issue of a healthy and sustainable diet. The food policy work brings all the pieces together in terms of land, seed, climate, and other citizen-related issues with a firm understanding of Farmer Managed Seed Systems (FMSS) as a foundation to justify diversity as a source of resilience.
The overall objective of the proposed initiative is to produce a food policy for Africa, which can serve as a framework for member countries, and suggest a governance structure to make it practical. The strategy to achieve this objective include mobilizing national food actors to influence their government to produce a national food policy and advocate for an African Food Policy and use the process and outcomes to facilitate citizens' engagement in local, national, and regional food system-related issues. It is assessed that AFSA's intervention is regional in scope that utilizes country-level initiatives and influence to leverage impact at scale across various other countries other than the selected nine African countries.

The Alliance for Food Sovereignty in Africa (AFSA) är en bred allians som består av aktörer från civilsamhället vilka ingår bland de parter som kämpar för livsmedelssuveränitet och agroekologi i Afrika. AFSA är ett nätverk av nätverk och är för närvarande aktiva i 35 medlemsländer.
Insatsen syftar till att påverka beslutsfattares narrativ för livsmedelspolicyer lokalt och regionalt genom påverkansarbete som i sin tur ska säkra att livsmedelspolicyer styrs av de afrikanska invånarnas hälsa och välmående i första hand. Insatsen utgår från AFSAs tidigare arbete och skiftar fokus från produktion av mat till att mera systematiskt även inkludera en hälsosam och hållbar diet. AFSAs arbete sammanför alla delar av livsmedelspolicyn såsom mark, utsäde, klimatförändringar och andra medborgarrelaterade frågor och tillämpar Farmer Managed Seed Systems (FMSS) som en bas för att rättfärdiga diversitet som en källa för motståndskraft.
Insatsens övergripande mål är att ta fram en mat/livsmedelspolicy för Afrika, vilken kan utgöra ett ramverk för medlemsländerna samt att föreslå en styrningsstruktur för operationaliseringen. Strategin för att uppnå detta mål inkluderar en nationell mobilisering av livsmedelsaktörer för att påverka sina respektive regeringar att ta fram en nationell livsmedelspolicy, att förespråka en livsmedelspolicy för Afrika och att använda processen och resultaten till att möjliggöra medborgarnas engagemang för lokala, nationella och regionala livsmedelsrelaterade frågor. Sida bedömer att AFSAs insats är regional till sin omfattning och drar nytta av initiativ på landnivå samt har påverkan i en större skala dvs utöver de nio utvalda länderna.

The purpose of Alliance for Food Sovereignty in Africa's (AFSA's) three-year intervention is to inspire African citizens to demand and consume healthy and culturally appropriate food backed by favorable policies. It is assessed that AFSA has developed a strategy to influence food policy makers' narratives and public thinking locally and regionally through advocacy and campaign ensuring that food policies are geared towards the health and well-being of African citizens. AFSA's contribution has four specific objectives 1) Advocate for developing and implementing regional and national policies that promote the production and consumption of healthy foods, especially indigenous African diets. 2) Create a cohesive and influential civil society coalition committed to behavioral and policy change regarding healthy food consumption. 3) Influence citizens' attitudes toward consuming healthy African foods and diets. 4) Establish mechanisms for regular feedback from the community and stakeholders to assess the impact of advocacy efforts and ensure alignment with the primary objective.

description.narrative:
The contribution implemented by AFSA and its implementing partners is charting a new path toward equitable and climate resilient food systems in Africa, through embedding agroecology in education, legislation, and public discourse, and by equipping local actors with the tools and platforms to lead. Multisectoral partnerships and grassroots engagement approach has been identified as instrumental tool to influence policy and social attitudinal change.
The contribution continues to serve as a dynamic force in reshaping Africas food systems through a people centered, agroecological, and policy driven approach. By advancing food sovereignty, promoting healthy and culturally appropriate diets, and strengthening grassroots movements, TAFS has built a continental momentum for lasting change. The establishment of multistakeholder platforms, national alliances, and policy dialogues has not only elevated the visibility of agroecology but also improved coordination among smallholder farmers, civil society, researchers, and policymakers across the continent.
The increasing knowledge among Africans on the harm of processed foods has prompted a notable shift in public perceptions towards traditional African diets. Various initiatives across the continent have successfully raised awareness about the nutritional benefits and cultural significance of indigenous foods. Intermediate results highlight country specific efforts that showcase the growing recognition of traditional diets in Africa. The contribution is emerging as a pivotal initiative in establishing a robust network of food systems actors across Africa, uniting a diverse array of stakeholders, including farmers, policymakers, researchers, civil society organizations (CSOs), and consumers. This collaborative effort served as a springboard to promote agroecology, advocate for food sovereignty, and drive policy reforms, challenging industrial food systems and fostering sustainable, localized solutions to food security. The post Malabo policy discussions have provided a strategic opportunity to institutionalize agroecology and food sovereignty within Africa's agricultural policies. Non-state actors, particularly AFSA, have advocated for a more inclusive approach in shaping the continent's food and agriculture agenda for the next decade.
